classification.difficultyReason: Infer the square's side from the inscribed circle's diameter, calculate both areas and simplify their exact ratio.

content.prompt: In the diagram opposite, the circle with radius $10\text{ cm}$ touches the insides of the square. Find the ratio of the area of the square to the area of the circle. Give your answer in terms of $\pi$.

spec.description: An unshaded circle inscribed in an unshaded square touches all four sides. A marked centre is joined horizontally to the right point of tangency, with the radius labelled 10 cm.
spec.mathematics: The square's side equals the circle's diameter. The given radius is 10 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied radius is labelled; calculated side lengths, areas and ratio remain hidden.

answer.short:
$4:\pi$

The square's side equals the circle's diameter; compare the two areas.
answer.worked:
The square's side equals the diameter because the circle touches each pair of opposite sides.
$$\begin{align*}s&=2\times10\\s&=20\text{ cm}\\A_{\text{square}}&=20^2\\A_{\text{square}}&=400\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{circle}}&=\pi\times10^2\\A_{\text{circle}}&=100\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
Dividing both terms of the ratio by $100$ gives
$$400:100\pi=4:\pi.$$
